description_good_justification: README.md opens with a one-line description: 'C2PA manifest embedding for WARC web archive files (ISO 28500).' Matches the GitHub repo description returned by `gh repo view` ('C2PA manifest embedding for WARC web archive files (ISO 28500)').
interact_justification: README.md documents install/obtain (crates.io, npm, pip) and usage. CONTRIBUTING.md explains how to give feedback/contribute (issues, PRs). SECURITY.md covers vulnerability feedback. GitHub Issues is enabled (`gh repo view` --json hasIssuesEnabled: true).
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Submitting Changes' section: fork the repo, branch from main, make changes with tests, run cargo test/clippy/fmt, open a PR. Explicit process.
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md specifies concrete acceptance requirements: `cargo test --all-features`, `cargo clippy --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and a Conventional Commits message style.
floss_license_justification: Cargo.toml: `license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"`. Both are FLOSS licenses; full texts present as LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE at repo root.
floss_license_osi_justification: Both MIT and Apache License 2.0 are OSI-approved licenses (OSI's approved-license list). LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE contain the unmodified standard license texts.
license_location_justification: LICENSE-APACHE and LICENSE-MIT hold the full texts (dual MIT OR Apache-2.0 per Cargo.toml); a top-level LICENSE file (identical to LICENSE-APACHE) is also present at the repository root for tooling that only recognizes that exact filename.
documentation_basics_justification: README.md documents overview, install for Rust/npm/Python, Quick Start with code examples for append_manifest/read_manifest, and an examples/ directory (examples/make_sample_warc.rs, examples/sample.warc).
documentation_interface_justification: Public API has rustdoc `///` comments (e.g. src/writer.rs `append_manifest`, src/reader.rs functions), src/lib.rs sets `#![warn(missing_docs)]` to enforce this, and docs are published to docs.rs (badge in README, `[package.metadata.docs.rs] all-features = true` in Cargo.toml).
sites_https_justification: Repo (https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-warc), crates.io, docs.rs, npm, and PyPI are all served over HTTPS; README badges link exclusively to https:// URLs.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues is enabled (`gh repo view` hasIssuesEnabled: true) and used for reports (issues #1-#16 observed via `gh api repos/writerslogic/c2pa-warc/issues`); publicly searchable, URL-addressable, no proprietary client required.
english_justification: README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, and all commit messages (`git log`) are in English.
maintained_justification: Active history: first commit 2026-05-14, most recent commit 6a9dffe on 2026-08-22, 26 commits total, latest CI runs green as of 2026-08-24 (`gh run list`). Single primary maintainer (David Condrey) with dependabot/aikido automation.
repo_public_justification: Public GitHub repo at https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-warc (`gh repo view` isPrivate: false).
repo_track_justification: git (`git log`) records author, timestamp, and message for every change, e.g. `git log --format='%an <%ae>'` and per-commit dates.
repo_interim_justification: Interim commits exist between and after tagged releases, e.g. 038e299, ea8847b between v0.2.0 (bc305b4) and v0.2.1, and dcab457/6a9dffe committed after v0.2.1 with no new tag yet.
repo_distributed_justification: Repository uses git, a distributed VCS.
version_unique_justification: Cargo.toml `version = "0.2.1"`; each release has a unique version identifier enforced by release.yml's 'Tag matches crate version' check.
version_tags_justification: `git tag -l` shows v0.2.0 and v0.2.1, matching Cargo.toml versions and GitHub releases (`gh release list`).
release_notes_justification: GitHub release v0.2.1's body is only '**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-warc/compare/v0.2.0...v0.2.1' (`gh api repos/writerslogic/c2pa-warc/releases/tags/v0.2.1`), and v0.2.0's body is an auto-generated 'What's Changed' list of Dependabot PR titles only, no human-curated summary of user-facing changes. cliff.toml (git-cliff config) is present but no CHANGELOG.md is committed and git-cliff is not wired into release.yml, so no curated release notes exist.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerabilities have been fixed in any release to date (no GitHub security advisories on the repo).
report_process_justification: GitHub Issues enabled; CONTRIBUTING.md 'Reporting Issues' section directs bug/feature reports to issue templates.
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues used for individual issues, observed via `gh api repos/writerslogic/c2pa-warc/issues` (issues #1 through #16).
report_responses_justification: No qualifying reports exist to assess a majority against (evidence: All issue-tracker activity to date is Dependabot dependency-bump PRs, consistently merged/closed promptly, e.g. #1 opened 2026-07-21 closed 2026-07-31, #6 opened and closed same day 2026-08-03, #12 opened 2026-08-10 closed 2026-08-17 (`gh api .../issues?state=closed`). No external human bug reports have been filed yet, so nothing is unaddressed.). Marked unknown rather than asserting a vacuous Met.
enhancement_responses_justification: No qualifying enhancement requests exist to assess a majority against (evidence: Same evidence as report_responses: no human enhancement requests filed to date; all automated dependency-update PRs are handled within days, so nothing is unaddressed.). Marked unknown rather than asserting a vacuous Met.
report_archive_justification: GitHub Issues provides a public, permanent, searchable archive of reports and responses at https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-warc/issues.
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md documents the process: private GitHub Security Advisory (https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-warc/security/advisories/new) or email admin@writerslogic.com, with expected response time and coordinated-disclosure request.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: SECURITY.md explicitly explains the private-report path (GitHub Security Advisories link or direct email), and states 'Please do not report security vulnerabilities through public GitHub issues.'
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports have been received to date (no security advisories exist on the repo), so there is no response-time data to evaluate.
build_justification: `cargo build` is the automated build; documented in CONTRIBUTING.md ('Development Setup') and exercised in CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml `check`, `test`, `msrv` jobs).
build_common_tools_justification: Uses Cargo, the standard Rust build tool, plus wasm-pack (npm build) and maturin (Python wheels via PyO3/maturin-action in release.yml) -- all standard tools for their respective targets.
build_floss_tools_justification: Cargo, rustc, clippy, rustfmt, wasm-pack, and maturin are all FLOSS; no proprietary build tooling is required.
test_justification: 12 `#[test]` functions across src/record.rs, src/reader.rs, src/writer.rs, and src/error.rs (`#[cfg(test)] mod tests` blocks), run via `cargo test`; documented in CONTRIBUTING.md and run in CI (ci.yml `test` job).
test_invocation_justification: `cargo test` is the standard test invocation for Rust; CONTRIBUTING.md documents this exact command.
test_most_justification: Existing tests cover the happy-path round-trip, multi-manifest handling, and 'last manifest wins' behavior, but src/record.rs implements explicit error branches for malformed input (unterminated header, missing/invalid Content-Length, body extending past end of data, non-UTF-8 header) that have no corresponding tests -- grep for 'empty|truncat|invalid|corrupt|malformed' in src/*.rs found these paths only in production code, not in any `#[test]` function.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: .github/workflows/ci.yml `test` job runs `cargo test` on every push and pull_request to main.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Submitting Changes' step 2: 'Make changes, add tests, run `cargo test --all-features`.'
tests_are_added_justification: Commit 0e7db6b ('feat: uniform Error::code, verified MSRV, and integration tests') adds tests alongside the functional change to src/error.rs; the 12 existing `#[test]` functions track with the feature commits that introduced the corresponding modules (record.rs, reader.rs, writer.rs).
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Submitting Changes' step 2 explicitly documents the add-tests requirement as part of the contribution process.
warnings_justification: CI runs `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo clippy --features python -- -D warnings`, and `cargo clippy --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -- -D warnings`, plus `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (.github/workflows/ci.yml `check` job).
warnings_fixed_justification: `gh run list -R writerslogic/c2pa-warc --limit 8` shows the CI `check` job (which includes the -D warnings clippy invocations) completing with status 'success' on recent runs through 2026-08-24, confirming no outstanding warnings block merges.
warnings_strict_justification: `-D warnings` (deny-level) is applied across default, python-feature, and wasm32 target/feature combinations in ci.yml, and src/lib.rs adds `#![warn(missing_docs)]` on top of clippy -- close to maximal practical strictness for a multi-target crate.
know_secure_design_justification: SECURITY.md documents a supply-chain security policy (GitHub Actions pinned to full commit SHAs, OpenSSF Scorecard and Dependabot in CI). src/lib.rs has `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`. Commit dcab457 'ci(security): pin actions by SHA and drop GITHUB_TOKEN to read' shows deliberate privilege reduction in CI.
know_common_errors_justification: src/record.rs's WARC parser explicitly guards against malformed/untrusted byte input, returning `Error::InvalidRecord` for unterminated headers, missing/invalid Content-Length, and body-extends-past-end-of-data rather than panicking or indexing out of bounds, combined with `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` and security-labeled fix commits (b26f53b 'fix(security): bump pyo3 to 0.29', c539ca8 'fix(security): autofix 3rd party Github Actions should be pinned').
crypto_published_justification: c2pa-warc has zero dependencies (Cargo.toml `[dependencies]` is empty) and implements no cryptography; it stores/retrieves opaque C2PA manifest-store byte blobs inside WARC records without inspecting, signing, or verifying their contents. Signing/verification is the caller's/C2PA SDK's responsibility, not this crate's.
crypto_call_justification: No cryptographic functionality is implemented in this crate; see crypto_published_justification.
crypto_floss_justification: No cryptographic functionality is implemented in this crate; see crypto_published_justification.
crypto_keylength_justification: No cryptographic functionality is implemented in this crate; see crypto_published_justification.
crypto_working_justification: No cryptographic functionality is implemented in this crate; see crypto_published_justification.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No cryptographic functionality is implemented in this crate; see crypto_published_justification.
crypto_pfs_justification: No cryptographic functionality is implemented in this crate; see crypto_published_justification.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The crate handles no passwords or user credentials; see crypto_published_justification.
crypto_random_justification: No cryptographic functionality is implemented in this crate; see crypto_published_justification.
delivery_mitm_justification: Package distribution is via crates.io/npm/PyPI over HTTPS, and source is cloned via SSH/HTTPS git (`git remote -v` shows `git@github.com:writerslogic/c2pa-warc.git`).
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hash-only integrity check is retrieved over plain HTTP; all package registries (crates.io, npm, PyPI) serve over HTTPS, and PyPI publishing uses OIDC Trusted Publishing (release.yml `pypi` job, no static token).
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No open unpatched medium+ severity vulnerabilities were found; recent security-labeled commits (b26f53b pyo3 bump, c539ca8 Actions pinning) show prompt remediation and no open GitHub security advisories exist for the repo.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: Aikido-flagged 'Actions should be pinned' issue (#6, opened 2026-08-03) was closed the same day per `gh api .../issues?state=closed`.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: Grep of src/ for api-key/secret/password/token patterns (`grep -rniE "(api[_-]?key|secret|password|token)\s*=..."`) found no matches; no secrets observed in README, CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, workflow files, Cargo.toml, or src/*.rs.
static_analysis_justification: `cargo clippy` (FLOSS static analysis for Rust) runs in CI on every push/PR across default/python-feature/wasm32-target combinations (.github/workflows/ci.yml `check` job) and again in release.yml before publishing.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: Clippy's default lint set covers correctness/style issues but no vulnerability-focused scanner is configured: no `cargo audit`/`cargo-deny` found, and scorecard.yml's `codeql-action/upload-sarif` step only uploads OpenSSF Scorecard's own SARIF output -- there is no CodeQL `init`/`analyze` job in any workflow.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: CI enforces `-D warnings` on all clippy invocations, so findings block merge; `gh run list` confirms recent `check` job runs are green (status 'success').
static_analysis_often_justification: ci.yml triggers clippy `on: push` and `pull_request` to branches: [main], i.e. on every commit.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No dynamic analysis tool (e.g. cargo-fuzz, Miri, AddressSanitizer/ThreadSanitizer) was found configured in CI or elsewhere in the repo.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The codebase is Rust with `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` declared in src/lib.rs; no memory-unsafe C/C++ code is present.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: No dynamic-analysis configuration exists at all (see dynamic_analysis), so there is no assertion configuration to evaluate.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis tool is run against this project (see dynamic_analysis), so there are no dynamic-analysis findings to fix.
